{{Short description|Indian mathematician and computer scientist (born 1964)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2022}}
{{Use Indian English|date=November 2022}}
[[File:Tamal Krishna Dey, Ohio State University.jpg|thumb|Tamal K. Dey at the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|MFO]], 2012]]
'''Tamal Krishna Dey''' (born 1964){{r|born}} is an Indian mathematician and computer scientist specializing in [[computational geometry]] and [[computational topology]]. He is a professor at [[Purdue University]].{{r|purfac}}

==Education and career==
Dey graduated from [[Jadavpur University]] in 1985, with a bachelor's degree in electronics. He earned a master's degree from the [[Indian Institute of Science Bangalore]] in 1987, and completed his Ph.D. at [[Purdue University]] in 1991.{{r|cv}} His dissertation, ''Decompositions of Polyhedra in Three Dimensions'', was supervised by [[Chandrajit Bajaj]].{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research with [[Herbert Edelsbrunner]] at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], Dey joined the Purdue faculty in 1992. He moved to the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur]] in 1994, and moved to the computer science and engineering department at [[Ohio State University]]<!--Wikipedians do not use "The" as part of Ohio State's name; it is considered a marketing gimmick, and routinely deleted.--> in 1999. At Ohio State, he obtained a courtesy appointment in the department of mathematics in 2015.{{r|cv}} He became the interim chair of the computer science department at Ohio State in 2019, before moving to Purdue in 2020.{{r|cv}}{{r|purfac}}

==Contributions==
Dey is known for proving the tightest-known [[upper bound]]s on the [[K-set (geometry)|{{mvar|k}}-set problem]]{{r|cg42}} and for his work on [[3D reconstruction]] and [[computational topology]].{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

He is the author of the book ''Curve and Surface Reconstruction: Algorithms with Mathematical Analysis'' (Cambridge University Press, 2006).{{r|csr}}
With Siu-Wing Cheng and [[Jonathan Shewchuk]], he is the co-author of ''Delaunay Mesh Generation'' (CRC Press, 2012).{{r|dmg}}

==Recognition==
Dey was elected as an [[ACM Fellow]] in 2018 for "contributions to computational geometry and computational topology".{{r|facm}} He is also a fellow of the [[IEEE]].{{r|cv}}
